walkthrough_label: Patient S1-D - on a blood thinner
reason_answer: To have my gallbladder taken out.

presentation.summary: Mr Imran, 67, has atrial fibrillation treated with apixaban and kidney function eGFR 68. When he last took apixaban decides whether surgery can proceed.

history.answer: Pain under the ribs after fatty food, on and off for a year.
Atrial fibrillation (irregular heartbeat), high blood pressure.
Apixaban for my heartbeat, and one blood pressure tablet.
No anaesthetic problems in the family.
Three days ago, as the pre-op nurse told me.
This morning. I forgot what the nurse said.

observations.note: Pulse irregular but rate 78: known, controlled atrial fibrillation.

examination.finding: Pulse irregularly irregular, rate about 78; heart sounds normal.

results.normal_range: 90 or above (60 to 89 is mildly reduced)
results.comment: Mildly reduced: enough for the usual apixaban pause
Known atrial fibrillation; confirms the pulse

scores.name: NEWS2
scores.note: Rate 78, other values normal; irregular rhythm is not scored by NEWS2

problems.label: Anticoagulant still active: bleeding risk at surgery
problems.why: Apixaban is usually omitted for a day or two before planned surgery with good kidneys. If he took it this morning, the drug is active and planned surgery is deferred.
expected_actions: Ask exactly when he last took apixaban
Decide: three days ago means proceed; this morning means defer and re-list
Tell the surgeon and the anaesthetist

decisions.prompt: He says: 'Three days ago, as the pre-op nurse told me.' What now?

options.text: Stopped long enough with good kidney function: proceed; restart after surgery as the surgeon decides
options.consequence: Variant D1 (PAUSE-type pause: 1 to 2 days with normal kidneys).

decisions.prompt: He says: 'This morning, I forgot.' What now?

options.text: The drug is still active: the surgeon and anaesthetist usually defer and re-list; reversal is not used just to make a planned operation possible
Proceed because the operation is minor
options.consequence: Bleeding risk with an active anticoagulant.

options.text: Give a reversal agent so surgery can go ahead

decisions.prompt: Pulse irregular, rate 78. What do you do?

options.text: Known, controlled atrial fibrillation: record it and confirm with an ECG
Treat it as a new emergency rhythm

correct: Ask exactly when he last took apixaban
D1: proceed; D2: defer and re-list
ECG to confirm known atrial fibrillation

incorrect.mistake: Does not ask when the last dose was
incorrect.shows: The anaesthetist asks at Sign In and finds a dose this morning

debrief.related: Anticoagulant, kidney function and timing go together
debrief.trigger_escalation: A dose within the pause window
debrief.remember: Ask exactly when the last tablet was taken

responsible_adult.text: My daughter will pick me up and sleep over at mine.

asa.why: Atrial fibrillation on a blood thinner is ASA 3 in the book's list of expected grades.
